title: Economics of production; cash flow in the production cycle
topicTitle: Economics of production; cash flow in the production cycle
notes: Economics of production asks whether a chemical process can be run at a cost the selling price will cover: raw materials, energy, labour, and the capital tied up in the plant.
Fixed costs, such as the plant and its depreciation, do not change with the day's output. Variable costs, such as feedstock and fuel, rise as more product is made.
The break-even output is the amount at which sales revenue equals fixed cost plus variable cost. Below that output the plant loses money even if the chemistry works.
Cash flow in the production cycle is the money moving out when materials are bought and moving in when the product is sold.

A long gap between purchase and sale locks cash in inventory and in unpaid invoices. A process can be chemically possible and still be rejected if energy and waste treatment cost more than the sales bring in.
